newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's bourse surges 30.6 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's bourse surges 30.6 pct in 1996.

text.p: Morocco's stock exchange index surged 30.6 percent in 1996 due to privatisation operations, steady rainfall and legal moves for more transparency, a Moroccan stockbroker said on Friday.

The Casablanca-based Upline Securities broker said in a 23-page report that issue of state equity-linked privatisation bonds and global depository receipts by Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, also boosted the market.
The all-share index rose to 447.13 points in 1996 from 342.29 points in the previous year.
Upline Securities Index, which tracks the 10 most liquid stocks, ended 1996 at 57.126 points from 41.929 points in 1995, up 36.2 percent.
The market capitalisation also jumped 50 percent to 76.2 billion dirhams ($8.3 billion) in 1996, up from 50.8 billion dirhams ($5.5 billion) in 1995.
Last year, the Moroccan government partly privatised oil refinery Samir, steel mill Sonasid, fertiliser firm Fertima FERT.CS. Private credit firm Credor was also floated on the stock exchange.
Upline said: "Growth also was due to the economy pickup following sustained rains and a drop of taxation on listed firms to 35 percent from 39.6 percent, except for credit firms and banks."
Eight banks and seven credit firms are listed on the stock exchange.
A slight drop of interest rates on long-term loans to 11.25 percent in 1996 from 12 percent in the previous year benefited notably credit and cement firms.

The authorities crackdown on smuggling, launched early last year influenced positively brewery firm Brasseries du Maroc, rubber company General tire and credit firms by curbing parallel distribution channels.
Despite the good results the report "deplores the market lack of liquidity" which inflates share prices compared with other emerging countries such as Egypt.
Total traded volume was 20.2 billion dirhams in 1996 against 23.2 billion dirhams in 1995, a bourse official said.
Upline said the bourse volume rose notably following the rush for mutual funds which collected more than 2.7 billion dirhams from 1.0 billion in 95, the report said.
Established in 1929, the Casablanca stock exchange has 47 listed stocks, and 22 mutual funds.
